disclaimer: Paper-trade tracking of a research rule. Not investment advice and not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. In our research, the corrected expected difference vs similar companies was about zero for Canadian names and roughly 1-2% a year for US names, with wide uncertainty. Backfilled positions are in-sample; the live record starts 2026-09-26.
research_notes: Correction (phase 3): an earlier portfolio engine overstated returns because daily rebalancing picked up bid-ask bounce; all numbers below use buy-and-hold weighting.
US base basket: about +1.5% a year (63-day hold, t 1.5) to +2.5% a year (126-day hold, t 2.7) vs matched peers after costs - a small, fragile difference.
Canadian buy baskets: about zero after costs (holdout -1.6% to +1.6% a year, not statistically significant).
Exits: leaving on an insider sale or company financing was about as good as a plain 252-day hold, not clearly better (2016-26 test: +1.6% vs +1.9% a year); the ledger keeps its original exit rule.

Market stress (S&P 500 more than 10% below its 1-year high, or VIX above 25): US insider buys did better in past stress periods, mostly 2008-09 and 2020; this is an expectation note, not a timing rule, and it did not replicate in Canada.

regime.label: NORMAL
regime.index_source: prices/SPY.json (S&P 500 ETF proxy for the index)
regime.note: Expectation note only, not a timing rule: in research, US insider buys disclosed in stressed markets (S&P >10% below its high or VIX > 25) did better than in calm ones, mostly because of 2008-09 and 2020; calm-market buys roughly matched peers after costs. Canada: no significant effect.

rules.entry: close of the first trading day after the filing date (live: after the later of filing date and the last close already past when first seen)
rules.base_filter: clean open-market buy (SEDI nature 10 / Form 4 P, not 10b5-1, not a flagged same-day same-price group); insider price/close 0.6-1.6; filed <= 10 days after trade; >= $10k USD; market cap >= $20M USD; stale-price share of last 63 sessions < 50%
rules.exit: first insider open-market SALE or company FINANCING filing (SEDI 11/15/16) filed after the buy -> close of the next trading day; else 252 trading days
rules.weighting: equal weight, one position per ticker; later qualifying buys in a held ticker are listed as additional insiders only

tags.tier_a: entry close at or below the insider price (tie-break tag only)
tags.caution: buy within 21 trading days after a company financing filing (soft downgrade)

limitations: Backfill (in-sample) uses today's shares outstanding for historical market caps and today's company catalog for peers (survivors); the live record decides with data available on the day.
US (Form 4) issuers have no financing filings on the tape, so their exits are insider sale or 252 days only.
USDCAD comes from Yahoo daily closes (bench/CAD=X.json (Yahoo USDCAD)).
Regime flag: S&P 500 (SPY proxy) drawdown > 10% from its 252-day high or VIX > 25 (bench/^VIX.json).
Descriptive track records contain forward returns measured after each buy; research found they do not predict later buys.

paper_pl.method: equal US$1,000 paper notional per position, simple sum (no compounding, no capital limit, overlapping positions all count); CAD listings translated to USD at implied USDCAD; open positions marked at last close; peer and SPY over the same windows
